#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One-time setup for the LetX promo audio pipeline.
#
# Everything runs locally — no API keys, no per-render cost, no licensing
# questions about the music or SFX (all of it is synthesized).
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")"

# --- system deps ------------------------------------------------------------
command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null || brew install ffmpeg
command -v espeak-ng >/dev/null || brew install espeak-ng

# Kokoro pulls in spaCy, which has no wheels for Python 3.14 (blis fails to
# build). 3.12 is the newest version that installs cleanly.
PY=$(command -v python3.12 || true)
[ -n "$PY" ] || { echo "need python3.12: brew install python@3.12"; exit 1; }

# --- venv -------------------------------------------------------------------
[ -d venv ] || "$PY" -m venv venv
./venv/bin/pip install -q --upgrade pip
./venv/bin/pip install -q numpy scipy soundfile kokoro

# --- espeak-ng data ---------------------------------------------------------
# The espeakng_loader wheel ships an incomplete data dir: no phontab/phondata,
# so misaki's phonemizer dies with
#   Error processing file '.../espeakng_loader/phontab': No such file
# espeak-ng also looks for those files in the loader dir itself, not in its
# espeak-ng-data/ subdir, so they get copied to both places.
LOADER=$(./venv/bin/python -c "import espeakng_loader,os;print(os.path.dirname(espeakng_loader.__file__))")
BREW_DATA=$(brew --prefix espeak-ng)/share/espeak-ng-data
cp -R "$BREW_DATA"/* "$LOADER/"
cp -Rn "$BREW_DATA"/* "$LOADER/espeak-ng-data/" 2>/dev/null || true

./venv/bin/python -c "import kokoro; print('kokoro ok')"
echo "setup complete — now run ./render.sh"

# Make a promo video with Claude Code

**Everything needed to produce a 30-second vertical promo video — animation,
voiceover, original music and sound effects — by prompting. No paid APIs, no
licensed music, no video editor, and zero marginal cost per render.**

This is the exact process and the exact scripts behind the promo for
[LetX](https://letx.app/), a collaborative LaTeX editor:

▶ **[Watch the result (30s)](https://youtube.com/shorts/CPx11OL0yMc)**
📖 **[Read the full write-up, with interactive prompt builder](https://shihub.online/blog/make-promo-video-with-claude-code)**

---

## What this is

Most "AI video" guides wire together three paid services. This one doesn't. The
animation comes out of Claude, and the entire soundtrack is generated locally:

| Piece | How | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Animation | Prompted, exported as MP4 | — |
| Voiceover | [Kokoro-82M](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M), running on your machine | free, unlimited re-renders |
| Music | Synthesized from scratch in numpy | free, nothing licensed |
| Sound effects | Synthesized from scratch in numpy | free, nothing licensed |
| Mix, master, mux | ffmpeg | free |

Because nothing is licensed, there is no attribution to track and nothing to
trip a content-ID match. Because the score is generated against your timeline
rather than trimmed to fit it, every cue lands on the exact frame you asked for.
And because the generator uses a fixed seed, renders are reproducible.

## You do not need to be a video editor

I am not one. The skill this actually requires is **writing a precise brief**.
The prompts in [`prompts/`](prompts/) are the deliverable of this repo — the
code in [`pipeline/`](pipeline/) is what Claude Code wrote when given them.

## The five steps

| # | Step | Where | Prompt |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Write a timestamped scene sheet | Claude | [`prompts/01-scene-sheet.md`](prompts/01-scene-sheet.md) |
| 2 | Generate the animation | Claude | [`prompts/02-animation.md`](prompts/02-animation.md) |
| 3 | Write the voiceover as a timetable | Claude | [`prompts/03-voiceover.md`](prompts/03-voiceover.md) |
| 4 | Build the soundtrack | Claude Code | [`prompts/04-soundtrack.md`](prompts/04-soundtrack.md) |
| 5 | Check it, then ship | You | [`prompts/05-ship-checklist.md`](prompts/05-ship-checklist.md) |

Something breaks? [`prompts/fixes.md`](prompts/fixes.md) has a prompt for each
of the six failures that actually happened while making this video.

### The single most important idea

**Do not ask for a video first. Ask for the scene sheet.**

A video is thirty seconds of decisions — what appears, when, for how long, and
what sound lands on it. Ask for all of it at once and the model picks defaults
for every decision. Defaults are what "AI slop" is made of.

So step 1 produces a document: five scenes with exact start and end seconds.
Everything downstream keys off it. The voiceover is written into its gaps, the
music picks a tempo that lands on its cuts, and every sound effect is placed
against its boundaries.

In the LetX promo the cuts are at **3.0 / 8.0 / 19.0 / 25.0 seconds**, and every
audio cue in the video is defined relative to those four numbers. See
[`example/scene-and-cue-sheet.md`](example/scene-and-cue-sheet.md) for the
finished article — the full scene sheet, the voiceover script with timings, and
all ~90 cues.

## Running the pipeline

The scripts in [`pipeline/`](pipeline/) are the real ones that rendered the
video above, not a sanitized demo. They are tuned to one specific 30-second
video, so read them as a **worked example**: point Claude Code at them, describe
your video, and let it adapt them. That is faster and produces a better result
than trying to parameterize someone else's timeline.

```bash
cd pipeline
./setup.sh            # once: system deps + venv + Kokoro + espeak data fix
./render.sh           # score + VO + mix + master + mux  (~2 min, deterministic)
./render.sh af_bella  # same, different voice
```

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `synth.py` | Procedural score (120 BPM, Am–F–C–G) + ~90 SFX cues, arranged against the scene boundaries |
| `vo.py` | Kokoro-82M voiceover; one take per line, auto-fitted to its slot |
| `mix.py` | VO chain, sidechain ducking, bus glue, limiter |
| `build.sh` | Two-pass linear `loudnorm` + mux (video stream-copied) |
| `render.sh` | Runs all of the above |
| `splice-cta.sh` | Losslessly swaps one section between two renders — see below |

## Gotchas that cost me real time

- **Python 3.12.** Kokoro's dependency chain (misaki → spaCy → blis) has no
  wheels for 3.14; the install dies compiling `blis/py.pyx`.
- **espeak-ng data ships broken.** The `espeakng_loader` wheel has an incomplete
  data dir, so you get `Error processing file '.../phontab': No such file or
  directory`. Fix: copy Homebrew's `espeak-ng-data/*` into **both** the loader
  package dir and its `espeak-ng-data/` subdir — espeak looks in the package dir
  itself. `setup.sh` does this.
- **Two voice options, pick deliberately.** Local (Kokoro-82M) is free, private
  and unlimited. OpenRouter's `openai/gpt-audio` sounds better and costs about
  **$0.09 per 95s narration** — see `pipeline/vo_gpt.py`. If you use the API:
  audio output **requires** `stream: true` (a normal request 400s), the audio
  arrives as base64 chunks you concatenate, and there is no `speed` parameter,
  so an overlong line gets re-rendered with a pacing instruction rather than
  stretched. Send an identical persona prompt with every line or the voice
  drifts between takes.
- **macOS `say` is too robotic** — and the good system voices can't be scripted.
- **Never time-stretch a take to fit its slot.** Re-render it at a nudged speed
  instead. Stretching is exactly what makes synthetic voice sound synthetic.
- **Spell for the phonemizer, not for humans.** `.tex` → `dot tek`,
  `LetX` → `Let X`, `letx.app` → `Let X dot app`.
- **Two-pass `loudnorm` with `linear=true`.** Single-pass is dynamic: it pumped
  and overshot to **+0.4 dBTP**, which clips the moment a platform re-encodes.
- **Don't crush the bus before `loudnorm`.** An aggressive glue comp + limiter
  collapsed the loudness range to 1.2 LU and caused that overshoot. Leave ~3 dB
  of headroom and let the normaliser do the lift.
- **The venv is ~1.1 GB** (torch). Budget the disk once.

## Swapping one bad section, losslessly

A late re-render came back better everywhere except the last five seconds. Rather
than re-render everything, `splice-cta.sh` takes the body from one file and the
tail from the other.

This is a **stream copy** — zero re-encode, zero generation loss — which works
because both renders share a keyframe at exactly the cut point and identical
codec parameters. Check that before trusting it; the script prints what it did.

Before reusing a soundtrack on a *new* render, prove the timing matches instead
of assuming: cross-correlate per-frame brightness between the two files and
confirm a best-fit offset of 0 frames. `prompts/fixes.md` has the prompt.

## Publish numbers you can defend

The failure mode worth guarding against: a model will write a confident,
specific, entirely invented statistic, and a promo video is the worst place for
one — it gets embedded, reposted and screenshotted, and outlives any correction.

Two rules that came out of this:

1. **Derive claims from something queryable**, not an optional profile field. A
   self-reported country field was blank for most users and would have supported
   a far larger, completely unusable number than verified institutional email
   domains did.
2. **Round down.** Publish the round figure *below* the verified count. An "N+"
   claim never expires as you grow, so there is no reason to reach.

`prompts/05-ship-checklist.md` includes a prompt that audits every claim in your
video before you post it.

# The pipeline

These are the real scripts that rendered the
[LetX promo](https://youtube.com/shorts/CPx11OL0yMc), not a sanitized demo.

They are tuned to **one specific 30-second video**, with cue timings hard-coded
against its scene cuts at 3.0 / 8.0 / 19.0 / 25.0s. Read them as a worked
example rather than a general-purpose tool.

The fastest way to use them: point Claude Code at this directory, give it
`../prompts/04-soundtrack.md` filled in for your video, and let it adapt these
files. That produces a better result than trying to parameterize someone else's
timeline.

## Setup

```bash
./setup.sh     # system deps + venv + Kokoro + the espeak-ng data fix
./render.sh    # score + VO + mix + master + mux   (~2 min, deterministic)
```

`setup.sh` assumes macOS with Homebrew. On Linux, install `espeak-ng` and
`ffmpeg` from your package manager — the espeak data-copy step is usually
unnecessary there.

**Python 3.12 is required.** Kokoro's dependency chain (misaki → spaCy → blis)
has no wheels for 3.14 and the install dies compiling `blis/py.pyx`.

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `synth.py` | Procedural score (120 BPM, Am–F–C–G) + ~90 SFX cues, arranged against the scene boundaries. Fixed RNG seed — keep it, it's what makes renders reproducible. |
| `vo.py` | Kokoro-82M voiceover. One take per line, auto-fitted by nudging `speed` and re-rendering — never by time-stretching. |
| `mix.py` | VO chain (de-ess, EQ, two-stage compression, room), sidechain ducking, bus glue, limiter. |
| `build.sh` | Two-pass linear `loudnorm` to -14 LUFS / -1.5 dBTP, then mux with the video stream-copied. |
| `render.sh` | Runs all of the above. Takes a voice name: `./render.sh af_bella`. |
| `splice-cta.sh` | Losslessly swaps one section between two renders of the same video. |

## Paths

`render.sh` defaults to a source video and output directory from the original
project. Override them:

```bash
SRC=../my-video.mp4 OUTDIR=../out ./render.sh
```

"""
LetX promo — procedural score + SFX.

Everything here is synthesized from scratch (numpy), so the output is
100% licence-clean and every hit lands on an exact frame of the video.

Video: 1080x1920, 30fps, 30.000s.
Tempo: 120 BPM -> beat 0.5s, bar 2.0s. Scene cuts at 3.0 / 8.0 / 19.0 / 25.0
all land on beat or half-bar boundaries.
"""
import numpy as np
from scipy import signal
import soundfile as sf

SR = 48000
DUR = 30.0
N = int(SR * DUR)
T = np.arange(N) / SR

BPM = 120.0
BEAT = 60.0 / BPM          # 0.5s
BAR = BEAT * 4             # 2.0s

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)   # fixed seed -> reproducible render


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- utilities
def buf():
    return np.zeros(N, dtype=np.float64)


def idx(t):
    return int(round(t * SR))


def add(dst, src, at):
    """Mix `src` into `dst` starting at time `at` (seconds), clipped to length."""
    i = idx(at)
    if i >= N:
        return
    if i < 0:
        src = src[-i:]
        i = 0
    n = min(len(src), N - i)
    dst[i:i + n] += src[:n]


def adsr(n, a=0.005, d=0.1, s=0.0, r=0.1):
    """Simple ADSR over n samples."""
    a_n, d_n, r_n = int(a * SR), int(d * SR), int(r * SR)
    s_n = max(0, n - a_n - d_n - r_n)
    env = np.concatenate([
        np.linspace(0, 1, a_n, endpoint=False),
        np.linspace(1, s, d_n, endpoint=False),
        np.full(s_n, s),
        np.linspace(s, 0, r_n),
    ])
    return env[:n] if len(env) >= n else np.pad(env, (0, n - len(env)))


def expdecay(n, tau):
    return np.exp(-np.arange(n) / (tau * SR))


def lp(x, fc, order=2):
    fc = np.clip(fc, 20, SR / 2 - 100)
    b, a = signal.butter(order, fc / (SR / 2), 'low')
    return signal.lfilter(b, a, x)


def hp(x, fc, order=2):
    fc = np.clip(fc, 20, SR / 2 - 100)
    b, a = signal.butter(order, fc / (SR / 2), 'high')
    return signal.lfilter(b, a, x)


def bp(x, lo, hi, order=2):
    b, a = signal.butter(order, [lo / (SR / 2), hi / (SR / 2)], 'band')
    return signal.lfilter(b, a, x)


def sweep_lp(x, fc_curve, order=2):
    """Time-varying lowpass, done in 512-sample blocks (cheap and smooth enough)."""
    out = np.zeros_like(x)
    blk = 512
    zi = None
    for i in range(0, len(x), blk):
        fc = float(np.clip(fc_curve[min(i, len(fc_curve) - 1)], 40, SR / 2 - 200))
        b, a = signal.butter(order, fc / (SR / 2), 'low')
        if zi is None:
            zi = np.zeros(max(len(a), len(b)) - 1)
        seg, zi = signal.lfilter(b, a, x[i:i + blk], zi=zi)
        out[i:i + blk] = seg
    return out


def saw(freq, n, phase=0.0, harm=14):
    """Additive band-limited saw."""
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    out = np.zeros(n)
    for k in range(1, harm + 1):
        if freq * k > SR / 2.2:
            break
        out += np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * k * t + phase) / k
    return out * (2 / np.pi)


def sine(freq, n, phase=0.0):
    return np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * np.arange(n) / SR + phase)


def noise(n):
    return rng.standard_normal(n)


def reverb(x, decay=0.35, mix=0.25, predelay=0.02):
    """Cheap Schroeder-ish tail: a few delayed, filtered copies."""
    out = np.zeros(len(x) + int(SR * 1.2))
    out[:len(x)] = x
    taps = [(0.031, 0.75), (0.047, 0.66), (0.071, 0.58), (0.101, 0.5),
            (0.153, 0.4), (0.211, 0.3), (0.307, 0.2)]
    wet = np.zeros_like(out)
    for dt, g in taps:
        d = int((dt + predelay) * SR)
        seg = x * g * decay
        seg = lp(seg, 4200)
        n = min(len(seg), len(wet) - d)
        wet[d:d + n] += seg[:n]
        # second-order bounce
        d2 = d * 2
        n2 = min(len(seg), len(wet) - d2)
        if n2 > 0:
            wet[d2:d2 + n2] += seg[:n2] * decay * 0.5
    res = out + wet * mix
    return res[:len(x)]


def ramp(t0, t1, v0, v1, curve=1.0):
    """Piecewise gain curve helper -> full-length array segment writer."""
    g = np.zeros(N)
    i0, i1 = idx(t0), idx(t1)
    x = np.linspace(0, 1, max(1, i1 - i0)) ** curve
    g[i0:i1] = v0 + (v1 - v0) * x
    return g, i0, i1


def env_from_points(points, smooth=0.05):
    """points = [(time, value), ...] -> smoothed step/linear automation curve."""
    ts = np.array([p[0] for p in points])
    vs = np.array([p[1] for p in points])
    e = np.interp(T, ts, vs)
    w = max(3, int(smooth * SR))
    k = np.hanning(w)
    k /= k.sum()
    return np.convolve(e, k, mode='same')


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- note tables
def nt(name):
    """Note name -> Hz (A4 = 440)."""
    names = {'C': 0, 'C#': 1, 'D': 2, 'D#': 3, 'E': 4, 'F': 5, 'F#': 6,
             'G': 7, 'G#': 8, 'A': 9, 'A#': 10, 'B': 11}
    p, o = name[:-1], int(name[-1])
    return 440.0 * 2 ** ((names[p] + (o - 4) * 12 - 9) / 12)


# Am - F - C - G, one chord per bar, 4-bar loop = 8.0s (aligns with scene cuts)
PROG = [
    ('A', ['A2', 'C4', 'E4', 'A4']),
    ('F', ['F2', 'A3', 'C4', 'F4']),
    ('C', ['C3', 'E4', 'G4', 'C5']),
    ('G', ['G2', 'B3', 'D4', 'G4']),
]
ARP_SETS = [
    ['A4', 'C5', 'E5', 'C5', 'A4', 'E5', 'C5', 'G4'],
    ['F4', 'A4', 'C5', 'A4', 'F4', 'C5', 'A4', 'E5'],
    ['C5', 'E5', 'G5', 'E5', 'C5', 'G4', 'E5', 'C5'],
    ['G4', 'B4', 'D5', 'B4', 'G4', 'D5', 'B4', 'A4'],
]


# ================================================================== DRUMS
def kick():
    n = int(0.42 * SR)
    f = 130 * np.exp(-np.arange(n) / (0.022 * SR)) + 44
    ph = 2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR
    body = np.sin(ph) * expdecay(n, 0.14)
    click = hp(noise(int(0.006 * SR)), 1800) * 0.35
    out = body
    out[:len(click)] += click
    return np.tanh(out * 1.6) * 0.9


def snap():
    n = int(0.22 * SR)
    x = noise(n)
    x = bp(x, 1400, 6500) * expdecay(n, 0.045)
    tone = sine(320, n) * expdecay(n, 0.03) * 0.25
    return (x * 0.7 + tone) * 0.55


def hat(open_=False):
    n = int((0.16 if open_ else 0.045) * SR)
    x = hp(noise(n), 7200) * expdecay(n, 0.05 if open_ else 0.014)
    return x * (0.24 if open_ else 0.2)


def rim():
    n = int(0.09 * SR)
    x = bp(noise(n), 900, 3000) * expdecay(n, 0.018)
    return x * 0.35


# ================================================================== SFX
def ui_tick(pitch=1900, level=0.34):
    """Crisp UI click — used for the filename stack."""
    n = int(0.09 * SR)
    tone = (sine(pitch, n) + 0.5 * sine(pitch * 2.01, n)) * expdecay(n, 0.012)
    click = hp(noise(int(0.004 * SR)), 4000) * 0.5
    out = tone * 0.8
    out[:len(click)] += click
    return lp(out, 12000) * level


def impact(level=1.0, bright=1.0):
    """Cinematic slam — sub drop + noise burst + short tail."""
    n = int(1.6 * SR)
    f = 120 * np.exp(-np.arange(n) / (0.05 * SR)) + 34
    sub = np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR) * expdecay(n, 0.32)
    crack = lp(noise(n), 5000 * bright) * expdecay(n, 0.09) * 0.5
    body = bp(noise(n), 120, 900) * expdecay(n, 0.2) * 0.35
    x = np.tanh((sub * 1.1 + crack + body) * 1.3)
    return reverb(x, decay=0.3, mix=0.3) * 0.85 * level


def whoosh(dur=0.55, level=0.5, rise=True, lo=250, hi=6000):
    """Filtered noise sweep — transitions, wipes, swipes."""
    n = int(dur * SR)
    x = noise(n)
    curve = np.linspace(0, 1, n) ** 0.7
    fc = lo + (hi - lo) * (curve if rise else curve[::-1])
    x = sweep_lp(x, fc, order=2)
    x = hp(x, 180)
    env = np.sin(np.pi * np.linspace(0, 1, n)) ** 1.4
    return x * env * level


def swish(dur=0.26, level=0.3):
    """Small object moving — the attachment chips."""
    n = int(dur * SR)
    x = bp(noise(n), 700, 5200)
    env = np.sin(np.pi * np.linspace(0, 1, n)) ** 2
    return x * env * level


def key_click(level=0.16, pitch=2600):
    """Mechanical-ish keystroke, deliberately soft so it sits under the VO."""
    n = int(0.05 * SR)
    tone = sine(pitch * (0.9 + 0.2 * rng.random()), n) * expdecay(n, 0.006)
    body = bp(noise(n), 1200, 7000) * expdecay(n, 0.009)
    return (tone * 0.35 + body * 0.65) * level


def ping(freq=1320, level=0.4, dur=1.1, decay=0.28):
    """Bell-ish confirmation tone — compile chip, stat hits."""
    n = int(dur * SR)
    parts = [(1.0, 1.0, decay), (2.0, 0.4, decay * 0.6),
             (3.01, 0.18, decay * 0.4), (4.98, 0.09, decay * 0.3)]
    x = np.zeros(n)
    for mult, amp, tau in parts:
        x += sine(freq * mult, n) * expdecay(n, tau) * amp
    x *= adsr(n, a=0.002, d=0.02, s=0.85, r=dur * 0.7)
    return reverb(x, decay=0.35, mix=0.22) * level


def thud(level=0.55):
    """Something lands."""
    n = int(0.6 * SR)
    f = 90 * np.exp(-np.arange(n) / (0.03 * SR)) + 52
    sub = np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR) * expdecay(n, 0.12)
    body = lp(noise(n), 1400) * expdecay(n, 0.05) * 0.4
    return np.tanh((sub + body) * 1.2) * level


def riser(dur=2.2, level=0.35, f0=180, f1=2400):
    """Tension riser — noise + rising detuned tone."""
    n = int(dur * SR)
    t = np.arange(n) / SR
    curve = (t / dur) ** 1.8
    f = f0 + (f1 - f0) * curve
    tone = np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR)
    tone += 0.6 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f * 1.005) / SR)
    nz = sweep_lp(noise(n), 400 + 9000 * curve)
    x = tone * 0.35 + nz * 0.5
    return x * (curve ** 1.2) * level


def reverse_swell(dur=1.0, level=0.4):
    """Reverse-cymbal style pull-in before a hit."""
    n = int(dur * SR)
    x = hp(noise(n), 900)
    env = np.linspace(0, 1, n) ** 2.5
    return x * env * level


def freeze_stop(level=0.6):
    """Record-stop / everything-freezes gesture."""
    n = int(0.9 * SR)
    f = np.linspace(700, 60, n)
    tone = np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR) * expdecay(n, 0.22)
    nz = sweep_lp(noise(n), np.linspace(9000, 250, n)) * expdecay(n, 0.18) * 0.5
    return np.tanh((tone + nz) * 1.1) * level


# ================================================================== MUSIC BED
def build_music():
    sub_b, arp_b, pad_b, drum_b, tex_b = buf(), buf(), buf(), buf(), buf()

    # ---- pad: sustained chord stack, one per bar, long overlapping tails
    for bar_i in range(int(DUR / BAR) + 1):
        t0 = bar_i * BAR
        if t0 >= DUR:
            break
        _, notes = PROG[bar_i % 4]
        n = int((BAR * 1.9) * SR)
        chord = np.zeros(n)
        for j, name in enumerate(notes[1:]):
            f = nt(name)
            for det in (-0.14, 0.0, 0.15):
                chord += saw(f * (1 + det / 100), n, phase=rng.random() * 6.28,
                             harm=8) * (0.5 / (j + 1.6))
        chord = lp(chord, 1500)
        chord *= adsr(n, a=0.55, d=0.4, s=0.55, r=BAR * 1.0)
        add(pad_b, chord * 0.20, t0)

    # ---- sub bass: root note, eighth-note pulse with a long first hit
    for bar_i in range(int(DUR / BAR) + 1):
        t0 = bar_i * BAR
        if t0 >= DUR:
            break
        root = nt(PROG[bar_i % 4][1][0])
        pattern = [0.0, 1.0, 1.5, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5]  # in beats
        for b in pattern:
            n = int(0.42 * SR)
            x = (sine(root, n) * 0.8 + sine(root * 2, n) * 0.18
                 + saw(root, n, harm=5) * 0.12)
            x *= adsr(n, a=0.004, d=0.16, s=0.35, r=0.2)
            add(sub_b, lp(x, 420) * 0.5, t0 + b * BEAT)

    # ---- arp: 16th plucks, the "premium dev tool" signature
    step = BEAT / 2
    total_steps = int(DUR / step)
    for s in range(total_steps):
        t0 = s * step
        bar_i = int(t0 // BAR) % 4
        note = ARP_SETS[bar_i][s % 8]
        f = nt(note)
        n = int(0.36 * SR)
        x = saw(f, n, harm=10) * 0.5 + sine(f * 2, n) * 0.18
        x = lp(x, 2600 + 900 * np.sin(t0 * 0.7))
        x *= expdecay(n, 0.055) * (1.0 if s % 2 == 0 else 0.62)
        add(arp_b, x * 0.17, t0)

    # ---- drums
    for bar_i in range(int(DUR / BAR) + 2):
        t0 = bar_i * BAR
        if t0 >= DUR:
            break
        for b in (0, 1, 2, 3):                      # four on the floor
            add(drum_b, kick(), t0 + b * BEAT)
        for b in (1, 3):                            # backbeat snap
            add(drum_b, snap(), t0 + b * BEAT)
        for h in range(8):                          # eighth hats
            add(drum_b, hat(open_=(h == 7)), t0 + h * (BEAT / 2))
        if bar_i % 4 == 3:                          # bar-end rim fill
            for r in (3.5, 3.75):
                add(drum_b, rim(), t0 + r * BEAT)

    # ---- texture: slow filtered-noise "air" so no frame is dead silent
    air = sweep_lp(noise(N), 600 + 500 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 0.07 * T))
    air = hp(air, 300)
    tex_b += air * 0.012

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ arrangement
    # Gains keyed to the exact scene boundaries of the video.
    g_pad = env_from_points([
        (0.0, 0.55), (2.1, 0.55), (2.2, 0.9), (3.0, 0.7), (5.35, 0.7),
        (5.45, 1.05), (7.95, 0.6), (8.05, 0.95), (18.9, 0.95), (19.1, 0.8),

        (7.9, 0.18), (8.05, 1.0), (15.5, 1.0), (15.7, 0.85), (18.9, 0.85),
        (19.1, 0.45), (22.9, 0.5), (23.1, 0.9), (25.0, 0.8), (28.0, 0.6),
        (30.0, 0.2),
    ], smooth=0.05)

    g_drum = env_from_points([
        (0.0, 0.0), (2.95, 0.0), (3.05, 0.30), (5.3, 0.42), (5.45, 0.0),
        (7.95, 0.0), (8.05, 1.0), (18.9, 1.0), (19.1, 0.55), (22.9, 0.55),
        (23.1, 0.85), (25.0, 0.9), (27.6, 0.75), (28.6, 0.35), (29.4, 0.0),
    ], smooth=0.04)

    # Global filter automation: dark during the "freeze/paywall" beat,

    fc = env_from_points([
        (0.0, 2600), (2.2, 6000), (3.0, 5000), (5.35, 5200), (5.5, 620),

# ================================================================== STEREO
def widen(x, amount=0.35, delay_ms=9.0):
    """Haas widening — keeps the low end mono, spreads the top."""
    d = int(SR * delay_ms / 1000)
    low = lp(x, 180)
    high = x - low
    l = high.copy()
    r = np.concatenate([np.zeros(d), high[:-d]]) if d else high.copy()
    l = low + l * (1 + amount)
    r = low + r * (1 + amount)
    return np.stack([l, r], axis=1)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# LetX promo — mux the finished mix onto the silent render.
#
# Video is stream-copied (no re-encode, no quality loss).
# Audio uses TWO-PASS loudnorm in linear mode: pass 1 measures, pass 2 applies
# a single static gain. Single-pass loudnorm is dynamic — it pumps, and it
# overshot to +0.4 dBTP here, which clips once a platform re-encodes.
set -euo pipefail

SRC="${SRC:-/Users/shahriar/github/letx-marketing/LetX Promo.mp4}"
MIX="$1"
OUT="$2"
I="${I:--14}"        # integrated target (LUFS)
TP="${TP:--1.5}"     # true-peak ceiling (dBTP)
LRA="${LRA:-7}"

# ---- pass 1: measure -------------------------------------------------------
MEAS=$(ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostats -i "$MIX" \
  -af "loudnorm=I=$I:TP=$TP:LRA=$LRA:print_format=json" \
  -f null - 2>&1 | awk '/^\{/,/^\}/')

get() { echo "$MEAS" | grep "\"$1\"" | sed 's/.*: *"\(.*\)".*/\1/'; }
MI=$(get input_i); MTP=$(get input_tp); MLRA=$(get input_lra)
MTH=$(get input_thresh); MOFF=$(get target_offset)
echo "measured: I=$MI TP=$MTP LRA=$MLRA thresh=$MTH offset=$MOFF"

# ---- pass 2: apply + mux ---------------------------------------------------
ffmpeg -y -v error \
  -i "$SRC" -i "$MIX" \
  -filter_complex "[1:a]loudnorm=I=$I:TP=$TP:LRA=$LRA:\
measured_I=$MI:measured_TP=$MTP:measured_LRA=$MLRA:\
measured_thresh=$MTH:offset=$MOFF:linear=true:print_format=summary,\
aresample=48000:resampler=soxr:precision=28[a]" \
  -map 0:v -map "[a]" \
  -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 256k -ar 48000 -ac 2 \
  -movflags +faststart -shortest \
  "$OUT"

echo "wrote $OUT"
ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostats -i "$OUT" -af ebur128=peak=true -f null - 2>&1 \
  | grep -E "^ *(I|LRA|Peak): *-?[0-9]" | sed 's/^/  final /'

"""
LetX explainer — voiceover via OpenRouter `openai/gpt-audio`.

Why not Kokoro (which the 30s promo uses): gpt-audio's decoder is markedly more
natural, and at roughly $0.004 per line a full 95 s render costs about $0.06 —
cheap enough to re-render freely while tuning timing.

Two API quirks worth knowing:
  * Audio output **requires** `stream: true`. A non-streaming request 400s with
    "Audio output requires stream: true".
  * Audio arrives as base64 PCM chunks on `delta.audio.data`, 24 kHz mono.

Fitting lines to their slots: gpt-audio has no `speed` parameter, so instead of
time-stretching (which is exactly what makes TTS sound synthetic) we escalate a
pacing instruction and re-render. Same principle as the promo's Kokoro path.

Usage:  python vo_gpt.py [voice] [out.wav]
"""
import base64
import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

import numpy as np
import soundfile as sf
from scipy import signal

SR_TTS = 24000
SR = 48000
DUR = 95.0
URL = 'https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions'
MODEL = 'openai/gpt-audio'

VOICE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'marin'
OUT = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else f'vo_{VOICE}.wav'

# The persona is sent with every line. Keeping it identical across lines is what
# holds the voice consistent — gpt-audio drifts if the framing changes.
PERSONA = (
    "You are the voiceover artist for a polished software product explainer. "
    "Warm, confident, unhurried, genuinely enthusiastic without being salesy. "
    "You sound like a real person who uses and believes in this product — not "
    "an announcer, not an advert. Speak the line as a complete thought with "
    "natural sentence-final intonation."
)

# `text` is spelled for the speech model, not for humans:
#   "Lay-tek"  -> LaTeX, said the way its users say it (never "latex")
#   "Let X"    -> LetX
#   "Let X dot app" -> letx.app
# (start, text, max_len)
LINES = [
    (0.60,  "Tired of clunky Lay-tek setups?",                                  3.4),
    (5.35,  "Meet Let X — collaborative Lay-tek, right in your browser.",        4.4),
    (10.30, "No installs. Just start writing, for free.",                        3.5),
    (14.45, "Sign in in seconds. Zero config.",                                  3.4),
    (19.45, "Keep every project organized — or import straight from GitHub, or a zip.", 5.9),
    (26.40, "Choose from over a thousand templates, ready to go.",               4.8),
    (32.45, "Write together in real time. No conflicts, no version clashes.",    6.2),
    (40.45, "Compile in seconds. No paywalls, no waiting.",                      5.6),
    (48.45, "Meet your A I assistant — like Cursor, for papers. "
            "Ask it to write a section, and watch it generate right in your editor.", 11.0),
    (61.45, "Editor, templates, A I, and P D F — all in one platform.",          5.4),
    (68.70, "Loved by students and faculty who've made the switch.",             7.2),
    (78.45, "Built by researchers, for researchers.",                            5.2),
    (85.70, "Start writing, free — at Let X dot app.",                           7.4),
]

# Escalating pace nudges, used only when a take overruns its slot.
PACE = [
    "",
    " Speak at a slightly brisker pace than usual, still relaxed.",
    " Speak briskly and efficiently, but keep it natural.",
    " Speak quickly and tightly, without sounding rushed or clipped.",
]


def say(text, voice, extra=''):
    """One take. Returns float32 mono at SR_TTS, plus the reported cost."""
    body = {
        'model': MODEL,
        'modalities': ['text', 'audio'],
        'audio': {'voice': voice, 'format': 'pcm16'},
        'stream': True,
        'messages': [{'role': 'user',
                      'content': f'{PERSONA}{extra}\n\nSay only these words:\n{text}'}],
    }
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        URL, data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
        headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {os.environ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"]}',
                 'Content-Type': 'application/json'})

    chunks, cost = [], 0.0
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as r:
        for raw in r:
            line = raw.decode().strip()
            if not line.startswith('data: '):
                continue
            payload = line[6:]
            if payload == '[DONE]':
                break
            try:
                ev = json.loads(payload)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
            if ev.get('usage'):
                cost = ev['usage'].get('cost', 0.0)
            for ch in ev.get('choices') or []:
                a = (ch.get('delta') or {}).get('audio')
                if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get('data'):
                    chunks.append(base64.b64decode(a['data']))

    pcm = np.frombuffer(b''.join(chunks), dtype='<i2').astype(np.float32) / 32768.0
    return pcm, cost


def trim(x, thresh=0.010, pad_head=0.010, pad_tail=0.05):
    """Strip the dead air the model leaves at both ends."""
    win = max(1, int(0.005 * SR_TTS))
    e = np.convolve(np.abs(x), np.ones(win) / win, mode='same')
    nz = np.where(e > thresh)[0]
    if len(nz) == 0:
        return x
    i0 = max(0, nz[0] - int(pad_head * SR_TTS))
    i1 = min(len(x), nz[-1] + int(pad_tail * SR_TTS))
    return x[i0:i1]


def main():
    if not os.environ.get('OPENROUTER_API_KEY'):
        sys.exit('OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set — source the repo .env first')

    track = np.zeros(int(SR_TTS * (DUR + 6)), dtype=np.float32)
    report, total = [], 0.0

    for start, text, maxlen in LINES:
        best = None
        for attempt in range(len(PACE)):
            au, cost = say(text, VOICE, PACE[attempt])
            total += cost
            au = trim(au)
            dur = len(au) / SR_TTS
            if best is None or dur < best[1]:
                best = (au, dur, attempt)
            if dur <= maxlen:
                break
        au, dur, attempt = best
        if dur > maxlen:
            print(f'  ! {start:6.2f} still {dur:.2f}s > {maxlen:.2f}s slot', file=sys.stderr)

        f = int(0.008 * SR_TTS)
        au = au.copy()
        au[:f] *= np.linspace(0, 1, f)
        au[-f:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, f)

        i = int(start * SR_TTS)
        track[i:i + len(au)] += au
        report.append((start, dur, start + dur, attempt, text))

    track = track[:int(SR_TTS * DUR)]
    track = signal.resample_poly(track, SR // 1000, SR_TTS // 1000)
    sf.write(OUT, track, SR, subtype='PCM_24')

    print(f'voice={VOICE}  ->  {OUT}   cost=${total:.3f}')
    print(f"{'start':>6} {'len':>5} {'end':>6} {'try':>4}  line")
    for s, d, e, a, t in report:
        print(f'{s:6.2f} {d:5.2f} {e:6.2f} {a:4d}  {t[:64]}')
    speech = sum(d for _, d, _, _, _ in report)
    print(f'\nspeech {speech:.1f}s of {DUR:.0f}s ({speech / DUR * 100:.0f}%)')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""
LetX promo — voiceover render (Kokoro-82M, local).

Each line is generated on its own so Kokoro produces natural sentence-final
prosody, then auto-fitted: if a take overruns its slot we nudge `speed` and
re-render rather than time-stretching (stretching is what makes TTS sound
robotic).

Timings are locked to the video's scene boundaries: 3.0 / 8.0 / 19.0 / 25.0.
"""
import sys
import numpy as np
import soundfile as sf
from scipy import signal

SR_TTS = 24000
SR = 48000
VOICE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'af_heart'
OUT = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'vo.wav'
DUR = 30.0

# (start, text, max_len, base_speed)
# `text` is spelled for the phonemizer, not for humans:
#   "dot tek"  -> .tex the way LaTeX users actually say it
#   "Let X"    -> LetX
LINES = [
    # --- Scene 1: the hook -------------------------------------------------
    (0.45,  "We've all been here.",                          1.60, 0.96),
    (2.28,  "Stop emailing dot tek files.",                  1.90, 1.00),
    # --- Scene 2: the problem ----------------------------------------------
    (4.30,  "Version chaos.",                                1.05, 1.02),
    (5.70,  "Add a collaborator? Pay up.",                   1.85, 1.02),
    # --- Scene 3: the product ----------------------------------------------
    (8.30,  "Let X is different.",                           1.35, 0.98),
    (9.60,  "Two cursors. One document. Live.",              2.45, 0.99),
    (12.20, "Compiles in seconds.",                          1.45, 0.98),
    (13.55, "Drag your whole project in. It just opens.",    2.65, 1.01),
    (16.45, "Over a thousand publisher ready templates.",    2.60, 1.01),
    # --- Scene 4: proof ----------------------------------------------------
    (19.90, "Used in universities across forty plus countries.", 2.70, 1.00),
    (23.15, "Unlimited collaborators. Free.",                2.20, 0.94),
    # --- Scene 5: CTA ------------------------------------------------------
    (26.10, "Let X dot app.",                                1.35, 0.95),
    (27.55, "No installation. Drag your project in.",        2.35, 0.99),
]


def trim(x, thresh=0.012, pad_head=0.012, pad_tail=0.06):
    """Strip the dead air Kokoro leaves at both ends."""
    a = np.abs(x)
    win = int(0.005 * SR_TTS)
    e = np.convolve(a, np.ones(win) / win, mode='same')
    nz = np.where(e > thresh)[0]
    if len(nz) == 0:
        return x
    i0 = max(0, nz[0] - int(pad_head * SR_TTS))
    i1 = min(len(x), nz[-1] + int(pad_tail * SR_TTS))
    return x[i0:i1]


def render(pipe, text, speed):
    chunks = [a.output.audio.numpy() for a in pipe(text, voice=VOICE, speed=speed)]
    return trim(np.concatenate(chunks))


def main():
    from kokoro import KPipeline
    pipe = KPipeline(lang_code='a')

    track = np.zeros(int(SR_TTS * (DUR + 3)))
    report = []

    for start, text, maxlen, base in LINES:
        speed = base
        for attempt in range(6):
            au = render(pipe, text, speed)
            dur = len(au) / SR_TTS
            if dur <= maxlen or attempt == 5:
                break
            # overran the slot — speak a little quicker, re-render clean
            speed = min(1.35, speed * (dur / maxlen) ** 0.65)
        i = int(start * SR_TTS)
        # short fades so nothing clicks at the seams
        f = int(0.008 * SR_TTS)
        au[:f] *= np.linspace(0, 1, f)
        au[-f:] *= np.linspace(1, 0, f)
        track[i:i + len(au)] += au
        report.append((start, round(dur, 2), round(start + dur, 2),
                       round(speed, 3), text))

    track = track[:int(SR_TTS * DUR)]

    # 24k -> 48k to match the music/SFX beds
    track = signal.resample_poly(track, SR // 1000, SR_TTS // 1000)

    sf.write(OUT, track, SR, subtype='PCM_24')

    print(f'voice={VOICE}  ->  {OUT}')
    print(f"{'start':>6} {'len':>5} {'end':>6} {'spd':>5}  line")
    for s, d, e, sp, t in report:
        print(f'{s:6.2f} {d:5.2f} {e:6.2f} {sp:5.2f}  {t}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""
LetX promo — final mix.

  VO   : HPF, de-ess, presence EQ, compression, gentle saturation, small room
  Music: ducked under the VO (sidechain), high-shelf carved where speech lives
  SFX  : lightly ducked, kept punchy

Output is a 48 kHz stereo master; loudness is normalised to -14 LUFS by the
ffmpeg step in build.sh (the social-platform target).
"""
import sys
import numpy as np
import soundfile as sf
from scipy import signal

SR = 48000
VO_PATH = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'vo_af_heart.wav'
OUT = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'mix.wav'


def read(path):
    x, sr = sf.read(path, always_2d=True)
    assert sr == SR, f'{path}: {sr}'
    return x.T  # -> (channels, n)


def to_stereo(x):
    return np.vstack([x, x]) if x.shape[0] == 1 else x


def biquad(x, b, a):
    return signal.lfilter(b, a, x, axis=-1)


def hpf(x, fc, order=2):
    b, a = signal.butter(order, fc / (SR / 2), 'high')
    return biquad(x, b, a)


def lpf(x, fc, order=2):
    b, a = signal.butter(order, fc / (SR / 2), 'low')
    return biquad(x, b, a)


def peaking(x, fc, gain_db, q=1.0):
    """RBJ peaking EQ."""
    A = 10 ** (gain_db / 40)
    w0 = 2 * np.pi * fc / SR
    alpha = np.sin(w0) / (2 * q)
    b = [1 + alpha * A, -2 * np.cos(w0), 1 - alpha * A]
    a = [1 + alpha / A, -2 * np.cos(w0), 1 - alpha / A]
    return biquad(x, np.array(b) / a[0], np.array(a) / a[0])


def highshelf(x, fc, gain_db, q=0.707):
    A = 10 ** (gain_db / 40)
    w0 = 2 * np.pi * fc / SR
    alpha = np.sin(w0) / (2 * q)
    c, s = np.cos(w0), np.sqrt(A)
    b = [A * ((A + 1) + (A - 1) * c + 2 * s * alpha),
         -2 * A * ((A - 1) + (A + 1) * c),
         A * ((A + 1) + (A - 1) * c - 2 * s * alpha)]
    a = [(A + 1) - (A - 1) * c + 2 * s * alpha,
         2 * ((A - 1) - (A + 1) * c),
         (A + 1) - (A - 1) * c - 2 * s * alpha]
    return biquad(x, np.array(b) / a[0], np.array(a) / a[0])


def envelope(x, attack=0.005, release=0.12):
    """Mono peak follower with separate attack/release."""
    m = np.abs(x).max(axis=0) if x.ndim > 1 else np.abs(x)
    ka = np.exp(-1 / (attack * SR))
    kr = np.exp(-1 / (release * SR))
    out = np.empty_like(m)
    e = 0.0
    for i in range(len(m)):
        v = m[i]
        k = ka if v > e else kr
        e = k * e + (1 - k) * v
        out[i] = e
    return out


def compress(x, thresh_db=-20, ratio=3.5, attack=0.006, release=0.12, makeup_db=0):
    env = envelope(x, attack, release)
    env_db = 20 * np.log10(np.maximum(env, 1e-9))
    over = np.maximum(0.0, env_db - thresh_db)
    gain_db = -over * (1 - 1 / ratio) + makeup_db
    g = 10 ** (gain_db / 20)
    return x * g


def deess(x, fc=6800, thresh=0.12, amount=0.65):
    """Split the sibilant band and compress only that."""
    b, a = signal.butter(2, [5200 / (SR / 2), 11000 / (SR / 2)], 'band')
    sib = biquad(x, b, a)
    env = envelope(sib, 0.001, 0.045)
    red = np.clip(thresh / np.maximum(env, 1e-9), 0, 1)
    red = 1 - (1 - red) * amount
    return x - sib * (1 - red)


def reverb(x, mix=0.10, decay=0.22, predelay=0.018):
    """Small, dry room — just enough that the VO isn't stuck to the speaker."""
    n = x.shape[-1]
    wet = np.zeros_like(x)
    taps = [(0.0113, 0.7), (0.0197, 0.55), (0.0291, 0.45),
            (0.0431, 0.35), (0.0619, 0.26), (0.0893, 0.18)]
    for dt, g in taps:
        d = int((dt + predelay) * SR)
        if d >= n:
            continue
        wet[..., d:] += x[..., :n - d] * g * decay
    wet = lpf(hpf(wet, 400), 5200)
    return x + wet * mix


def saturate(x, drive=1.4, blend=0.35):
    return x * (1 - blend) + np.tanh(x * drive) / np.tanh(drive) * blend


def duck(target, control, depth_db=-11.0, attack=0.012, release=0.28,
         thresh=0.02, lookahead=0.05):
    """
    Sidechain: pull `target` down wherever `control` (the VO) is speaking.
    Lookahead means the duck opens *before* the word, not on top of it.
    """
    env = envelope(control, attack, release)
    la = int(lookahead * SR)
    env = np.concatenate([env[la:], np.zeros(la)])
    act = np.clip((env - thresh) / 0.10, 0, 1) ** 0.6
    w = int(0.03 * SR)
    k = np.hanning(w)
    k /= k.sum()
    act = np.convolve(act, k, mode='same')
    gain = 10 ** ((depth_db * act) / 20)
    return target * gain


def limit(x, ceiling=0.97, lookahead=0.003):
    la = int(lookahead * SR)
    m = np.abs(x).max(axis=0)
    m = np.concatenate([m[la:], np.zeros(la)]) if la else m
    env = envelope(np.vstack([m, m]), 0.0005, 0.06)
    g = np.minimum(1.0, ceiling / np.maximum(env, 1e-9))
    w = int(0.004 * SR)
    k = np.hanning(w)
    k /= k.sum()
    g = np.convolve(g, k, mode='same')
    return np.tanh(x * g / ceiling) * ceiling


def main():
    vo = to_stereo(read(VO_PATH))
    music = to_stereo(read('music.wav'))
    sfx = to_stereo(read('sfx.wav'))

    n = min(vo.shape[-1], music.shape[-1], sfx.shape[-1])
    vo, music, sfx = vo[:, :n], music[:, :n], sfx[:, :n]

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- VOICE
    v = hpf(vo, 95, order=3)          # kill rumble/DC
    v = peaking(v, 260, -2.2, q=1.1)  # de-mud
    v = peaking(v, 1900, 1.6, q=0.9)  # intelligibility
    v = peaking(v, 4200, 2.8, q=0.8)  # presence / "in the room"
    v = highshelf(v, 9000, 1.8)       # air
    v = deess(v, thresh=0.10, amount=0.7)
    v = compress(v, thresh_db=-21, ratio=3.2, attack=0.005, release=0.11,
                 makeup_db=5.5)
    v = compress(v, thresh_db=-12, ratio=2.4, attack=0.001, release=0.05,
                 makeup_db=2.0)       # second, faster stage = broadcast glue
    v = saturate(v, drive=1.6, blend=0.30)
    v = reverb(v, mix=0.09)
    v = v / max(1e-9, np.abs(v).max()) * 0.80

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- MUSIC
    m = music
    m = peaking(m, 2400, -3.4, q=0.7)   # carve a pocket where speech lives
    m = peaking(m, 55, 2.0, q=0.9)      # keep the sub weight on phone speakers
    m = highshelf(m, 11000, 1.2)
    m = duck(m, v, depth_db=-11.5, release=0.30)
    m = m * 0.30

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ SFX
    s = sfx
    s = peaking(s, 3000, -1.8, q=0.8)
    s = duck(s, v, depth_db=-4.5, release=0.22)
    s = s * 0.46

    bus = v + m + s
    # Light glue only — loudnorm does the loudness lift downstream, and
    # crushing here collapses LRA and pushes inter-sample peaks over 0 dBTP.
    bus = compress(bus, thresh_db=-11, ratio=1.6, attack=0.015, release=0.22,
                   makeup_db=1.0)
    bus = limit(bus, ceiling=0.89)

    sf.write(OUT, bus.T, SR, subtype='PCM_24')

    peak = 20 * np.log10(np.abs(bus).max())
    rms = 20 * np.log10(np.sqrt((bus ** 2).mean()))
    print(f'{OUT}: {n / SR:.2f}s  peak {peak:.2f} dBFS  rms {rms:.2f} dBFS')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
